summary: Lane B2 is a SOURCE-KIND ruling (T25) only — no anchors, no continue points, no type changes, so target rows 1-12 take neither an anchor nor an anchor_hostile entry. The finding: the anime adapts the TAPAS WEBCOMIC of The Beginning After the End (story TurtleMe, art Fuyuki23 for seasons 1-5, Tapas Entertainment / Yen Press in print; Piccoma in Japan), not TurtleMe's web novel. The decisive evidence is the anime's own credit block, which carries an English line verbatim: 'Based on the comic series, created by TurtleMe and published by Tapas Entertainment' (official site caststaff page; reproduced independently by Animate Times alongside 原作：TurtleMe / ストーリー監修：TurtleMe). The stored anchors confirm the space: they are in the WEBCOMIC's own chapter numbering (1-243+), not the novel's — tbate.fandom's webcomic chapter pages give ep 8's stored 39 = 'Happy Reunion' against anime ep 8 'Reunited with the King', and ep 12's stored 48-56 lands exactly on the webcomic's season-2 finale, ch 56 'All I Need'; the same webcomic ch 56 adapts NOVEL ch 29, so the novel space is a different, far coarser one. Recommendation: SOURCE_TYPE_OVERRIDES the-beginning-after-the-end → 'webtoon', NOT 'manhwa' — the work is an OEL American Tapas Original by a South-Korean-AMERICAN author, English-first, with no Korean publication of origin; 'manhwa' in our registry means countryOfOrigin KR and would assert something the sources do not support. AniList carries NO media entry for either the novel or the webcomic, so there is no ADAPTATION edge and derivation cannot produce a kind at all — an override is the only route.

structure.notes:
THE WORK (T25). Source = 'The Beginning After the End' WEBCOMIC — a Tapas Original, written by TurtleMe (Brandon Lee, a South-Korean-American writer), illustrated by Fuyuki23 (seasons 1-5) then MGK-Story (seasons 6-present), first published on Tapas 2018-07-07 and still running; print by Yen Press (11 volumes as of Aug 2026, en-WP); simultaneous licensed editions on KakaoPage (KR), Piccoma (JP, from 2020), Kuaikan (CN), Comico (TH), Delitoon (FR/DE). NOT the source: TurtleMe's WEB NOVEL of the same name, serialised on Tapas from 2017-01-18 — the webcomic adapts it, and the anime adapts the webcomic.

COUNT AND NUMBERING UNIT. Unit = webcomic CHAPTER, plain integers running across the comic's seven 'seasons'. tbate.fandom's TBATE Webcomic infobox: chapters = 243, seasons = 7, volumes = 10 (its Comic Chapters page shows a countdown to 'Chapter 244', so the run is live and the labels are 'Chapter N'). The wiki's per-unit pages are titled 'Episode N' but their body reads 'is the Nth episode of The Beginning After The End Webcomic' with the SAME N, and the Season chapter-list tables label the same units 'Chapter 26', 'Chapter 27'... — Episode N and Chapter N are one numbering.

NUMBERING TRAP (record this before anyone joins a chart). The webcomic carries TWO numberings and the fandom infobox prints both: `episode_webtoon` (= the page title N, the canonical chapter number) and `episode` (= the raw Tapas serial index, which counts prologues/notices/season breaks). Example: page 'Episode 48' has |episode = 57 |episode_webtoon = 48 — the Tapas index runs ~9 ahead by season 2 and grows. Our chapter space is the `episode_webtoon` / 'Chapter N' numbering. Never join on the `episode` field or on a Tapas URL index (R20).

THE TWO SPACES ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. tbate.fandom's webcomic pages carry `adapted_from` = the NOVEL chapter: wc1 → novel ch 1; wc5 'The Mana Core' → novel ch 4; wc13 'Sylvia' → novel ch 8; wc15 'Ones Held Dear' → novel ch 9; wc29 'Home' → novel ch 16; wc39 'Happy Reunion' → novel ch 21; wc45 'The Perfect Weapon' → novel ch 25; wc47 'Happy Birthday' → novel ch 26; wc48 'The Adventurer's Guild' → novel ch 27; wc56 'All I Need' (season-2 finale) → novel ch 29. So webcomic 1-56 ≈ novel 1-29: roughly 2 webcomic chapters per novel chapter. A number in one space read as the other is off by a factor of ~2.

WHICH SPACE THE STORED ANCHORS ARE IN. The 12 stored (afg) anchors — ep1→5[1], ep2→10[5], ep3→15[13], ep4→19[16], ep5→22[20], ep6→25[23], ep7→29[26], ep8→39[29]{29-32,39}, ep10→44[40], ep11→47[45]{34-37,45-47}, ep12→56[48] — sit in the WEBCOMIC space, on title evidence: anime ep 1 ends on the mana core and stored END 5 = wc5 'The Mana Core'; anime ep 3 'Meeting the King' and stored 13-15 = wc13 'Sylvia' … wc15 'Ones Held Dear'; anime ep 8 'Reunited with the King' and stored END 39 = wc39 'Happy Reunion'; anime ep 12 'The King's Departure' and stored 48-56 = wc48 'The Adventurer's Guild' … wc56 'All I Need', the webcomic's own season-2 finale. In the novel space ep 12 would sit near ch 29, not 56. The out-of-order chapters_adapted on eps 8 and 11 ({29-32, 39} and {34-37, 45-47}) are consistent with the anime restoring chronology the webcomic told with flashbacks — a rearranged annotation for an anchors lane, not this one.

ANILIST ADAPTATION EDGE — THERE ISN'T ONE. anime 183161 (source OTHER, JP) has exactly ONE relation: SEQUEL → 194317 (season 2, also source OTHER). No ADAPTATION edge, no manga node. Searching AniList MANGA for 'Beginning After the End', 'Saikyou no Ousama', 'TBATE' and 最強の王様 returns NO media entry for either the webcomic or the novel — AniList simply does not index this work outside the two anime entries. That is why the series stores 'other' and why deriveSourceKind cannot help: with no node there is no countryOfOrigin to refine by, so a SOURCE_TYPE_OVERRIDES ruling is the only path (T25 fail-closed).

THE ANIME'S OWN CREDIT. The official site's cast/staff page prints, verbatim, 'Based on the comic series, created by TurtleMe and published by Tapas Entertainment' (the page is JS-rendered; the string is in https://saikyo2dome-tbate.com/assets/js/app.js), and its INTRODUCTION describes the work as the SMARTOON® serialised on Piccoma from 2020 that won ピッコマAWARD 2021 and topped Tapas — i.e. the comic, not the novel. Animate Times reproduces the same block independently: 'Based on the comic series, created by TurtleMe and published by Tapas Entertainment / 原作：TurtleMe / 監督：元永慶太郎 / 構成：鴻野貴光 / ストーリー監修：TurtleMe / キャラクターデザイン：末岡正美 / 音楽：井内啓二 / アニメーション制作：studio A-CAT'. Note the 原作 line names TurtleMe only — he wrote BOTH works, so that line alone is ambiguous; the 'comic series … published by Tapas Entertainment' sentence is what disambiguates it.

GAP TO RECORD. tbate.fandom's anime episode tables (Template:List of Season 1 Episodes) have an 'Adapted From' column that is EMPTY for all 12 season-1 rows — the fan wiki does not map the anime. Our per-episode mapping currently rests on AFG alone; an anchors lane on this series will need a second source (the webcomic chapter titles above are usable for title-level corroboration).

flags_for_sean: RECOMMENDATION (T25): SOURCE_TYPE_OVERRIDES['the-beginning-after-the-end'] = 'webtoon'. The registry already holds the record and needs no change: { value: 'webtoon', noun: 'webtoon', unit: 'chapter', tailBadge: 'webtoon only', anilistSources: [], aflAnimeCanon: 'filler', note: 'reserved — AniList has no WEBTOON manga format; enters only through SOURCE_TYPE_OVERRIDES' }. This is exactly the case the record was reserved for, and it would be its first use. Unit chapter is correct: our anchors are in the webcomic's chapter numbers.

WHY NOT 'manhwa' (this is the one place my verdict departs from the task's prior). 'manhwa' in SOURCE_KINDS is country-gated to KR. The Beginning After the End is NOT a Korean work: en-WP's short description is 'American web novel series and its adaptations', the article opens 'is an American web novel series written by TurtleMe', and its infobox is {{Infobox manhwa}} with OEL = y (original English-language). The webcomic is a Tapas Original, first published in English on a US platform, and the anime's own credit names 'Tapas Entertainment' as the publisher. The Korean KakaoPage edition is a licensed translation, not the origin. AniList has no node and therefore no countryOfOrigin to appeal to. Ruling 'manhwa' here would put a factual claim about origin into series identity that no source supports; 'webtoon' is format-true and origin-neutral. (Solo Leveling is the opposite case and I recommend 'manhwa' there — see solo-leveling.json.)

IF SEAN WANTS ONE BUCKET for both B2 webcomic series, the coherent single value is 'webtoon' for both (format-true for both, unit chapter for both, and it costs Solo Leveling only the KR signal). 'manhwa' for both is NOT available — it would be wrong on TBATE.

ALTERNATIVE rejected: 'web_novel' / 'light_novel'. Two reasons. (1) Evidence: the official credit says 'Based on the comic series … published by Tapas Entertainment'; ANN's announcement headline hedges ('Webnovel/Webcomic Gets TV Anime') and is not a credit. (2) Instrument: our registry gives web_novel unit = VOLUME, but this novel is a chapter-serial with no meaningful volume space (its 'volumes' are self-published Kobo e-book bundles), and our 12 stored anchors are chapter numbers ~2x the novel's — a web_novel ruling would make every stored anchor uninterpretable.

CONSEQUENCE OF THE RULING (worth a glance before applying): 'webtoon' has aflAnimeCanon = 'filler', identical to 'manga'/'manhwa', so nothing in the standing derivation moves. hasSource and hasInstrument both become TRUE (they are false today under 'other', unit none), so tail math, the strip and the 'webtoon only' badge switch on for this series. Our chapter space is currently total_chapters = null / total_volumes = null with no manga link — the tail cannot be computed until a chapter-space source is attached. The webcomic has no MangaUpdates-style node in our pipeline (AniList has none), so this may need a manual chapter-space entry: 243 chapters / 11 Yen Press volumes as of Aug 2026 (en-WP; tbate.fandom TBATE Webcomic infobox).
